title: Free sheaf shifted Hom computes derived module global sections
statement: Let $Z$ be any scheme and $\Lambda$ any commutative ring. Let $\Lambda_Z$ be the sheafification of the free $\Lambda$-module presheaf on the representable of the terminal object $\mathrm{id}_Z$ of the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], equivalently the constant rank-one module sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. For every integer $q\geq 0$ there is a natural isomorphism of functors on sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] to abelian groups, $F\mapsto \operatorname{Hom}_{D^+(Z_{\mathrm{Et}},\Lambda)}(\Lambda_Z[0],F[0][q])\cong F\mapsto U(H^q(R\Gamma(Z,F[0])))$, where $U$ forgets the module structure and cohomology and derived categories are as in [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] and [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories]. No compactness, separation, or torsion condition is imposed.

source.place: Tags 015A (definition-higher-derived-functors), 05TI (lemma-enough-injectives-right-derived), 070I (lemma-K-injective), and the equation after 03DI (equation-map-lower-shriek-OU-into-module); terminal object specialization and natural comparison written by J1

proof.text: Choose an injective resolution $F\to I^\bullet$ in the category of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules, using [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]. Its bounded-below injective complex is K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective]. Maps from $\Lambda_Z[0]$ to $F[0][q]$ are therefore degree-$q$ cohomology of the Hom complex from $\Lambda_Z[0]$ to $I^\bullet$, by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. The full inclusion of the bounded-below derived category preserves these Hom sets.

The free-sheaf sections equivalence, concretely Etale.freeSheafHomEquiv, identifies each term $\operatorname{Hom}(\Lambda_Z,I^n)$ with the underlying abelian group of $I^n(Z)$. This is the sheafified free-Yoneda adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-free-separator]. Naturality in $I^n$ identifies composition with its differential with the sections differential. Since $Z$ is terminal, evaluation is module global sections. The exact forgetful functor from modules to abelian groups preserves kernels, cokernels and homology, hence the Hom-complex cohomology is the underlying abelian group of $H^q(\Gamma(I^\bullet))$.

By [lem-sp-derived-functor-single-identification], the complex $\Gamma(I^\bullet)$ computes the module derived global sections of $F[0]$. A map of sheaves lifts to its injective resolutions. The termwise sections equivalence commutes with this lift by freeSheafHomEquiv_comp, so the induced comparison commutes with cohomology maps. Lifts are unique up to homotopy; homotopic maps induce the same cohomology maps by [lem-weil-pbc-homotopic-maps-equal-cohomology]. Package the additive component isomorphisms as a natural isomorphism. This argument requires no compactness, separation or torsion.

theorem nonempty_freeSheafDerivedSectionsIso (Z : Scheme.{u})
    (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ] (q : ℕ) :
    Nonempty
      ((DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor _ 0 ⋙ shiftFunctor _ (q : ℤ) ⋙
        preadditiveCoyoneda.obj
          (op ((DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor _ 0).obj
            ((Etale.freeSheaf Λ Z).obj
              (MorphismProperty.Over.mk ⊤ (𝟙 Z) (inferInstance : Etale (𝟙 Z))))))) ≅
        (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (Sheaf Z.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)) 0 ⋙
          Etale.cohomology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) Z (q : ℤ) ⋙
          forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}))
